<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via IApprovalService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class), IApprovalService (symbol, a top-level interface), approvals.getRecordLocks (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/approvals/records/:object/locks, selected by route anchor /approvals/records/:object/locks), getRecordLocks (sdk, the bare tail of client method approvals.getRecordLocks, bound to POST /api/v1/approvals/records/:object/locks), /approvals/records/:object/locks (route, bridged from symbol getRecordLocks — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/concepts/architecture.mdx`  _(via getSchema (literal, a string literal in detailRowsHeldByLockingApproval))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4b7b18b4f8409867bb356901a474d9c1c01df1a3` — the merge of head `584c26a0f89855639167544f105793bb35245fe1` into base `49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4b7b18b4f8409867bb356901a474d9c1c01df1a3 && git checkout 4b7b18b4f8409867bb356901a474d9c1c01df1a3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2 584c26a0f89855639167544f105793bb35245fe1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2 && git merge --no-ff 584c26a0f89855639167544f105793bb35245fe1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head 9b5bdcd8 · 2026-11-24T23:07Z

L1: REWORK (L1-w, zone wf-B)
Head-sha: `9b5bdcd81cdcab04bf7854606891135121ff7bb3`

The code is right. Two paper findings stand between it and ACCEPT, one of which moves a published docblock and so brings an L2.

### Must-fix

**M1. The published `getRecordLocks` docblock is made false by this PR.** `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` (shipped in `dist/*.d.ts`), `getRecordLocks`: "The same judgement, off the same snapshot, the record-lock `beforeUpdate` hook enforces." Before this PR that sentence described the batch read exactly: it asked `recordsHeldByLockingApproval` only. After it, the batch answers `locked: true` for a line whose master is held. No pending request sits on that line, and the record-lock hook does not refuse it; the detail-row lock hook does. So for that case the sentence is now false. The same omission already sits in the `getRecordLock` docblock above it ("`true` when a pending request on the record comes from a node whose `lockRecord` is not `false` — the same judgement … the record-lock `beforeUpdate` hook enforces"). It is pre-existing there, but `getRecordLocks` defers to it ("exactly what `getRecordLock` answers"), so fixing one sentence without the other leaves the two contradicting each other.
- Fix: one clause in each of the two docblocks saying that a master-detail line also answers `true` while its master is so held (the detail-row lock's judgement), as the plugin docblock and `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` ("Asked of a line, it answers `true` while the record the line belongs to is locked") already say. `locked` only stays: nothing in the #25934 ruling A's "what is answered" changes, only the condition for `true` is completed. `Clause-②: no` stays (no shape moves).
- This puts a non-test `packages/spec/src/**` path in the diff, so the new head owes an L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. I run it on that head. The claim's file surface names the spec docblock "only under route A", so **the seat** amends the claim first. Adjacent `getRecordLock` fix, four conditions: same defect class, mechanical, nobody else holds it, same gate family. All hold.

### Should-fix

**S1. The PR body's 维护者速读 still asks the maintainer to rule here.** Its last bullet, "要你做的：裁定行菜单"删除"按钮的取舍…", predates the seat's routing call. That question now lives on #37151, and this PR lands the parity fix alone. As written, the maintainer reads this PR as waiting on them. Fix: point the bullet at #37151 (or say nothing is asked of the maintainer here). It is a body patch by the card thread through relay `issue_patch` and does not move the head.

### Read and found right (head 9b5bdcd8)

- `l1-face.mjs --pr 37145`: CLEAN, 13 items. Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #37041` binds only this card, `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` match the edited claim 7145985823. The changeset names `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`. Floors are green, and so are all checks: 39 success, 18 expected skips, 0 failed, 0 pending. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **`Fixes` is right.** Both acceptance lines are met: batch parity without a read per row, plus a parity pin over held-itself, line-of-held-master and unheld. Seat 4's shape question (7145422785) is a separate card, #37151, carrying route A, route B and keep for the maintainer. It is not an unmet half of #37041.
- **Parity.** `getRecordLocks` runs the detail half only on readable ids the record lock left unheld. That matches `getRecordLock`'s `recordHeld || detailRowHeld` short-circuit. Unreadable and missing ids still answer `null` from the untouched caller anchor, so the two cases stay indistinguishable. Repeated ids are deduped before every read and answered at each position.
- **`detailRowsHeldByLockingApproval`.** The bookkeeping guard comes first, and an object with no edge reads nothing. A single id keeps the one-row `{ id }` / `limit 1` shape. Many ids use `$in` with `limit = n`, under SYSTEM as before. Master ids are deduped per edge. Ids are compared as strings on both sides (`String(row.id)`, `String(record_id)`, `scalarFk`). One master goes through `pendingRequestFor` and several go through the `$in` path, and both fail open on a read error, so the batch and the single read agree there too. The master count never exceeds the readable rows, which already passed `PENDING_LOCK_LIMIT` (1,000) at the record half, and the door caps a call at 200 ids, so the batch adds no new refusal path. The one-row form's only caller is `getRecordLock`; the write hooks are untouched.
- **Tests.** Real commands with output (file 14/14, plugin suite 1922/1922, typecheck exit 0). One ablation on the tested line: the two new pins fail, everything else passes, and the restored blob equals HEAD. The read-count pin fixes the order `[line, sys_approval_request, line, sys_approval_request]` for an 8-row page. The parity pin covers three callers, a missing id, a repeated id, a self-held line and the unlock after a decision.
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence.** The batch read answered `false` while the single read answered `true` and the write was refused: matches the card's measurement. "One read of the rows' master-detail columns plus one lookup per master-detail edge … never one read per row": matches the code and the read-count pin. "The answer's shape is unchanged": yes. "A list page that reads the batch door now stops offering an editor on such a line": `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/hooks/useRowApprovalLocks.ts` reads the door for the select-first cells (`ObjectGrid.tsx` `hostCellSelection`). True.
- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` needs no edit. It already describes the batch read as the single read per id, and the single read as `true` for a line of a locked record. This PR makes that page true.

### Note (not a finding)

- With one row, `detailRowHeldByLockingApproval` now looks up every edge's master instead of returning at the first held one. The answer is the same and the read count is bounded by the edge count (usually 1).

### Path to ACCEPT

1. Seat: amend the claim's file surface to include the two `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` docblocks (M1).
2. Card thread: push the two-clause docblock fix (plus any regenerated spec artefact a gate asks for) and patch the body's 维护者速读 bullet (S1).
3. L1-w: delta read on the new head, and the L2 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record (claim line first) on the same head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `88b76bf8994f21d5c295326b5ba46adcf18532b0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts
Security-touching: yes

### ① Derived judgments

Read from the net diff `517e4153..88b76bf8` (5 files), not from the PR body.

- **`getRecordLocks` accept set: a readable master-detail line whose master carries a locking pending request moves from `{ locked: false }` to `{ locked: true }`.** Right. It is what `getRecordLock` answers for the same id on main, what the detail-row lock hook (`bindDetailRowLockHook`) refuses on write, and what the batch docblock already promised ("exactly what `getRecordLock` answers for that id"). No other entry moves: an unreadable or missing id still answers `null` from the untouched caller anchor, a row held by its own request is answered by the first half and never reaches the second, and an object with no `master_detail` edge takes no extra read.
- **`getRecordLock` (single) accept set: meant to be unchanged; it is not quite.** `detailRowHeldByLockingApproval` now delegates to the batch form and answers `.has(recordId)`. Main answered from "the engine returned a row"; the head answers from "the returned row's id, as a string, equals the asked id". For every id spelled as stored the answer is identical. Where the datasource matches an id more loosely than string equality, the answer flips to `false`. Wrong in that corner: S1.
- **`detailRowHeldByLockingApproval` read count: the early return at the first held master is gone; every edge is now looked up.** Right. Same answer, bounded by the edge count, and the function's only caller is `getRecordLock`.
- **New export `detailRowsHeldByLockingApproval` in `lifecycle-hooks.ts`.** Module-internal: `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/index.ts` does not re-export `lifecycle-hooks`. No public surface is added. Right.
- **Spec docblocks: one clause in each of `getRecordLock` and `getRecordLocks`.** The condition for `true` is completed; the return types, the optionality, the `null` rule, the cap and the sentence "What is answered: `locked` only" do not move. Right. No type, schema, constant, route or wire payload changes anywhere in the diff.
- **Write path: unchanged.** `bindApprovalLockHook` and `bindDetailRowLockHook` are not in the diff; the hook still looks masters up one at a time through `lockingRequestsForRecords`.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/37041-batch-lock-detail-lines.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The level is right: a bug fix in a released package, nothing a metadata author can write changes, and no published shape widens or narrows.
- `Clause-②: no` is right. The answer stays `{ locked } | null` per entry; the docblock edit states a condition the implementation's single door already met.
- Package list: the diff also moves `@objectstack/spec` (the two docblocks ship in its `dist` declaration files) and the changeset does not name it. `.changeset/config.json` puts `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` in the one `fixed` group, so spec is versioned and published with this changeset either way; what is lost is a line in spec's own CHANGELOG. Graded N2, not a level error.
- Changeset body, sentence by sentence against the tree: the before/after answers, "one read of the rows' master-detail columns plus one lookup per master-detail edge ... never one read per row", and "the answer's shape is unchanged" all match the code. The gate verdict agrees: both `Check Changeset` runs on this head concluded success.

Check-runs on `88b76bf8`: 73 runs, every one success or skipped; none failed, none pending. Among them: Build Core, Test Core (all 10 shards and the roll-up), Test UI (all 16 shards and the roll-up), Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), every Lint lane, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, PR-body guards, Check Changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev report 7146721964, `open_questions[0]` (seat 4's constraint 7145422785: should the answer say which kind of lock holds the row, route A, or should the grid hide Delete on master-held lines, route B).** Answered for this head, escalated for the rest. This head takes neither route: it lands parity alone, and the shape stays `{ locked }`. That is the only option of the three that leaves the #25934 ruling A text ("What is answered: `locked` only") untouched, so it is the only one a seat may land without a ruling. Route A rewrites ruled text and widens a published return type; it is the maintainer's to rule. The PR body and the claim's seat edit say the question was moved to card #37151; I did not read that card (outside this brief's inputs) and take no position between A and B. On the contract's side, nothing in the spec text promises anything about delete: the promise is "never offers an edit the server will refuse", and the head makes that true for lines. The remaining gap (a refused Delete offer on a master-held line) exists on main and is not created here.
- **`security_findings: none`.** Agreed with one qualification, recorded under ④ (disclosure): no new class of disclosure, a wider door for an existing one.
- **`out_of_scope_findings: []`.** One to add, not this PR's: `getRecordLocks` anchors on `String(row.id)` equal to the asked id while `getRecordLock` anchors on "a row came back", so the two doors can already differ on main for a loosely matched id (`null` against `{ locked }`). Pre-existing and untouched by this diff; the seat may file it with S1.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5).** `detailRowsHeldByLockingApproval` reads the page's FK columns into the application, dedupes the master ids there and sends them back as an `$in` on `sys_approval_request`: an in-app semi-join, new at page scale (main did it for one row). No reason is written in the docblock, the changeset or the PR body for not asking the database to join. A reason does exist in the tree: the judgement (`nodeConfigLocksRecord` over the parsed `node_config_json` snapshot) is in-app by design and must be the one copy the write hook uses (`lockingRequestsForRecords`), the id set is bounded by the door's cap of 200, and the record half on main has the same shape. It is not stated where the next reader will look. Graded S2.

### ④ Design judgment

**Spec docblocks against the code and against ruling A.**

- `getRecordLock`, new sentence: "Asked of a master-detail line, it also answers `true` while the record the line belongs to is so held — the detail-row lock's judgement, which refuses the line's writes." True of the head: `getRecordLock` ORs `detailRowHeldByLockingApproval`, which judges each master through the same `lockingRequestsForRecords` the hook calls, and the hook refuses insert, update and delete. "So held" correctly limits it to a locking pending request on the master itself; a master that is only a line of a held grand-master is not held, in the read and in the hook alike (neither is transitive).
- The sentence sits inside the bullet "What is answered: `locked` only" and leaves that bullet's claim intact: the payload is still one boolean, and the line that follows ("No request id, node, participants or `pending` flag") is still true. Ruling A's text is completed, not changed.
- `getRecordLocks`, new clause: "and, for a master-detail line, the detail-row lock's: a line answers `true` while the record it belongs to is so held." True of the head, and it removes the falsehood the L1 named (the batch no longer answers from the record-lock hook's judgement alone).
- N1: both clauses say "the record the line belongs to" in the singular. `masterEdgesOf` counts every `master_detail` field, so a junction row answers `true` while any one of its masters is held.

**`getRecordLocks` against the contract, sentence by sentence.**

- "Entry `i` answers `recordIds[i]`", "a repeated id is answered at each of its positions": the final `ids.map` is positional over the undeduped list; every read uses the deduped `asked`. Holds.
- "`null` when it cannot or when it does not exist, never an entry that tells the two apart": the caller's `$in` read still runs first and alone decides `null`. Both later halves take only ids that read returned, and `heldByMaster` is consulted only behind `readableIds.has(id)`. An unreadable id and a missing id cause the same reads (none), so neither the answer nor the read pattern separates them. Holds.
- "The same judgement ... the record-lock hook enforces — and ... the detail-row lock's": first half `recordsHeldByLockingApproval`, second half `detailRowsHeldByLockingApproval`, both through `lockingRequestsForRecords` and `nodeConfigLocksRecord`. Holds.
- "A caller refused the object's read outright is refused the same way for every id": the anchor read throws before any other read. Holds.

**`detailRowsHeldByLockingApproval`, attempts to break it.**

- Several `master_detail` edges: one lookup per edge, results unioned; a row held through the second edge only is found. Two edges naming the same master object each get their own lookup. Holds.
- A master that is a bookkeeping object: `masterEdgesOf` drops the edge; `lockingRequestsForRecords` would also answer empty. A bookkeeping object asked as the detail: returns before any read. Holds.
- Duplicate ids: the service dedupes; a direct caller passing duplicates gets `limit` at or above the distinct count and a Set back. Holds.
- A page at the 200-id cap: at most 200 master ids per edge, under `PENDING_LOCK_LIMIT` (1,000), so the `lockedError` refusal in `pendingRequestsForRecords` cannot fire on the second half; a service caller past 1,000 ids is already refused by the first half, as on main. The lookup's row limit (1,001) cannot truncate, since `DUPLICATE_REQUEST` keeps one pending request per record. Holds.
- A read error on the masters' requests: one master goes through `pendingRequestFor`, several through the `$in` branch; both catch and answer empty, so the single read, the batch read and the hook all fail open together. A read error on the FK read throws out of both doors alike, as the single door did on main. Holds.
- A line held by its own request and by its master: answered `true` by the first half and filtered out of `unheld`. Holds.
- Numeric ids: the master side is normalised on both ends (`scalarFk` to string, `String(record_id)`), so a numeric FK matches a string `record_id`. The row side is where S1 lives.
- Batch against write hook: the hook exempts system sessions and the opening run's own writes; the read answers for the row, not for a writer. The docblocks on `detailRowHeldByLockingApproval` say so. Not a disagreement.

**Disclosure (the reason for `Security-touching: yes`).** The spec hunks teach what a caller who can read a line is told about another record: `locked: true` on a line says its master carries a locking pending approval, and the master's readability to that caller is not checked (the FK read and the request lookup are SYSTEM). This is not new at this head. The single door has answered it per id on main, and a writer learns it from the `RECORD_LOCKED` refusal. The batch door now answers it for up to 200 lines per request. What is disclosed is one bit per line; the master's id, the request, its node and its participants are not. The caller-anchor order is intact, so an unreadable row and a missing row stay indistinguishable. I find no new disclosure class and no must-fix here. The contract's "Who is answered" bullet does not say in words that reading the line is enough and the master need not be readable; with route A open on #37151, the ruling there should carry that sentence either way.

**Findings.**

S1 (should-fix) — `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts`, `detailRowHeldByLockingApproval`: `(await detailRowsHeldByLockingApproval(engine, objectName, [recordId])).has(recordId)` makes the single door's detail half depend on `String(row.id) === recordId`. Main took the row the engine returned for `where: { id }` and never compared ids. On a datasource that matches ids more loosely than string equality (a case-insensitive id collation, a numeric id column asked as `"07"`), the caller's anchor finds the row, the write hook refuses the line `RECORD_LOCKED`, and `getRecordLock` now answers `{ locked: false }` where main answered `true`. That is the defect class this card exists to remove, reintroduced in a corner of the door the diff meant to leave alone. Fix: the one-row form answers from the set's size (it asked one id, so a non-empty set is its answer), keeping the batch form as it is. Not measured on a live driver; read from the code, and it does not arise for an id spelled as stored, which is why it is not a must-fix.

S2 (should-fix) — `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts`, `detailRowsHeldByLockingApproval` docblock: the helper materialises master ids in the application and semi-joins by `$in` without saying why the join is not pushed down (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5). State the reason there in one sentence: the judgement is in-app over the `node_config_json` snapshot and must be the write hook's own `lockingRequestsForRecords`, and the id set is bounded by the door's 200-id cap. No code change is asked.
